newsitem.title: USA: US Plains fed cattle bid $65, asked $66 - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: US Plains fed cattle bid $65, asked $66 - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. feedlot cattle markets in the central and southern Plains were quiet early Thursday following light sales in those areas Wednesday at $65.00 per cwt, down $1.00 from last week, feedlot sources said.
A minimal number of heifers also sold at $66.50 in Kansas on Wednesday and in Nebraska, steers and heifers sold at $66.00.
Many of the 4,700 head sold in the Panhandle to major packers reportedly were being shipped early Thursday, which fueled ideas that packers were short-bought, sources said.

Packers were bidding $65.00 early, sources said, but most owners were resolved not to sell below $66.00. That resolve to hold out for $66.00 could be challenged by a sharp drop in beef prices Wednesday. However, hefty beef sales at the lower prices offset some of the bearishness, some sources noted.
Beef prices fell $0.89 to $1.20 per cwt by Wednesday's close, on 351 loads of fabricated cuts sold, USDA said.
"I'm going to sit tough and hope everyone else does the same," one Kansas feedlot manager said.
The heifers that brought $66.50 in Kansas reportedly were shipped to a Nebraska plant.
